rationale: Superseded by the re-review in docs/superpowers/tasks/2026-10-14-epmcdme-15555-hide-tool-outputs/code-review-final.json. CR-002 (workflow exemption) is resolved: is_workflow_conversation guards exist in strip_history_for_conversation and get_conversation_stream and are covered by tests (f83d60a41). CR-001 (resume ignores a version-pinned hide decision) is an accepted, documented gap (KNOWN GAP in _ask_assistant_resume, execution.py:269); it is not fixed in this MR. Original round-2 rationale: All 8 prior findings (CR-001 through CR-008) were verified fixed against current source: virtual-assistant filtering, per-message live-stream hiding, the Apache license header, fail-closed unparseable-line handling, the last-chunk-only error rescue, fail-closed deleted-assistant lookup, and strip_history(None) all now behave as the follow-up task describes. The standards audit's two blocking findings (missing license header; fail-open NDJSON parsing) do not reproduce against current source and are dismissed as stale for the same reason, though its standards_review rows are carried through unchanged per contract. 15 lens candidates were dismissed as stale/already-fixed or unreachable (chunk-splitting and unicode-decode edge cases do not apply because every caller yields one complete JSON-string chunk, never raw/split bytes; the unsupported-response-type fallback in strip_response is unreachable given the StreamingResponse|BaseModelResponse return-type contract on every call site). Two new issues remain: _ask_assistant_resume (assistant.py:1166) applies only the master assistant's hide flag, with no equivalent to _effective_hide_tool_outputs, so resuming a paused tool call on a version-pinned session can fail to hide outputs the pinned version marks hidden. Separately, the CR-002 fix removed the only is_workflow_conversation guard rather than adding it elsewhere, so all four history-serving boundaries now strip workflow conversations unconditionally, contradicting the spec's explicit non-goal that workflow-conversation messages are unaffected (business_review item 16, partial) — this needs a product/spec decision on which side of that contradiction to resolve. No findings were deferred.

findings.title: Resume endpoint skips version-pinned hide check
findings.problem: _ask_assistant_resume calls apply_to_response(assistant, handler.handle_tool_call_resume(...)) using only the master assistant record. Unlike ask_assistant_by_id/ask_assistant_by_slug, it never computes _effective_hide_tool_outputs(assistant, execution_assistant); _prepare_assistant_for_execution is explicitly skipped on this path ('resume reuses existing session context').
findings.impact: If the paused tool call being resumed runs against a version-pinned execution context whose pinned version has hide_tool_outputs=True while the current master assistant has it False, resuming will not hide outputs — bypassing the same fail-closed guarantee test_version_pin_cannot_bypass_hiding covers for the initial ask.
findings.recommendation: Resolve the execution assistant tied to the paused session (from the checkpoint/session context) and OR its hide_tool_outputs with the master's via _effective_hide_tool_outputs before calling apply_to_response, matching ask_assistant_by_id/by_slug.
findings.resolution: accepted-gap: documented as KNOWN GAP; not fixed in this MR

findings.title: Workflow conversations lose spec-mandated filtering exemption
findings.problem: The spec's non-goal states workflow-conversation messages are unaffected by hide_tool_outputs filtering. The CR-002 fix removed the only is_workflow_conversation guard (previously only on get_conversation_by_id) rather than adding an equivalent guard elsewhere; now get_conversation_by_id, get_conversation_stream, _with_stripped_history (delete/update/export) and the json export branch all call strip_history/strip_stream unconditionally, with no workflow guard anywhere in the file.
findings.impact: A workflow conversation containing a sub-assistant with hide_tool_outputs=True now has its thoughts stripped at every boundary, which is explicitly out of scope per spec. This resolves the prior inconsistency finding by trading one spec violation (inconsistent guard) for another (no guard at all), rather than reconciling with the stated non-goal.
findings.recommendation: Confirm with the spec/product owner whether workflow conversations should be fully exempt from this filtering (add a consistent is_workflow_conversation guard across all four boundaries) or whether the non-goal statement should be narrowed to agent-to-agent calls only (update spec and business_review accordingly).
findings.resolution: fixed in f83d60a41 (workflow exemption guards + tests)
